items.followUp: Define oscillatory motion and give one example.

rubric.why: The definition must identify back-and-forth motion about a central position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing motion to and fro about a mean position.

rubric.why: A suitable example completes the answer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any suitable example of vibratory motion.

modelAnswer: Vibratory motion is the to-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.
The vibrations of a tuning fork are an example.

items.followUp: State Newton's first law of motion and give two examples of it.

rubric.why: The law states that the forces are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that action and reaction are equal and opposite forces acting on different bodies.

rubric.why: The question requires two examples that illustrate the law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two suitable examples.

modelAnswer: When one body exerts a force on another body, the second body exerts an equal and opposite force on the first body; these forces act on different bodies.
Examples are gun recoil and walking.

items.followUp: What is meant by the normal reaction of a surface?

rubric.why: Tension is the pulling force associated with a stretched string.
rubric.description: Identifies tension as a pulling force in a stretched string.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing tension as the pulling force exerted by a stretched string.

rubric.why: The force acts along the string's length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that tension acts along the string.

modelAnswer: Tension is the pulling force exerted by a stretched string on an attached body.
It acts along the length of the string.
